current_difficulty_reason: Radial compactness by itself gives weak H1 and strong intermediate-Lp limits but can lose the prescribed L2 mass. The source controls the nonscale-invariant potentials through their local L3/2 and far-field uniform parts, passes the nonlinear equation to the limit and uses the positive limiting frequency to recover the entire mass. Only after that recovery and the energy identity does it promote the gradient convergence to strong H1 convergence, a remaining nonlocal perturbation obligation beyond the allowed radial compactness and Newton uniqueness foundations.
